headline: Idaho Hot Springs and Fire Lookout Permitting
reservation: Overnight stays in historic fire lookouts like Deadwood or Trinity Mountain must be reserved months in advance via recreation.gov. Most geothermal springs are day-use only, but nearby developed campgrounds may require advance booking during the summer rafting season. Verify all seasonal road openings and fire restrictions with the Boise National Forest supervisor's office.

days.title: Canyons and Hot Springs

stops.name: Kirkham Hot Springs
stops.detail: Soak in natural mineral pools with steaming waterfalls adjacent to the South Fork Payette River.

stops.name: Lowman Nature Pond
stops.detail: Observe local flora and birdlife in this accessible wetland area within the Ponderosa pine forest.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; Highway 21 is winding with potential wildlife; conditions vary.
days.note: Hot springs are fragile; use no soaps and respect day-use hours to protect the water quality.

days.title: Gold Rush History and High Ridges

stops.name: Idaho City Historic District
stops.detail: Walk through the 1860s gold rush town and visit the Boise Basin Museum.

stops.name: Mores Creek Summit
stops.detail: A high mountain pass offering access to various forest service trails and winter recreation areas.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; road conditions depend on seasonal maintenance.
days.note: Services in Idaho City are limited; ensure you have a full tank and water before heading deeper.

days.title: Whitewater and Wild Rivers

stops.name: Banks-Lowman Road
stops.detail: Drive the Wildlife Canyon Scenic Byway, watching for elk and eagles along the river banks.

stops.name: Main Payette River
stops.detail: Watch rafters navigate the whitewater or utilize public river access points for a picnic.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; watch for heavy boat-trailer traffic near Banks.
days.note: River conditions change rapidly with snowmelt; check flow rates at official USGS stations.

intel.title: Hot Spring Staging
intel.text: Parking at Kirkham is strictly regulated and fills fast on weekends. Avoid parking on the highway shoulder to prevent citations and safety hazards.

intel.title: Deep Canyon Limits
intel.text: Radio and cellular signals are absent once you enter the South Fork canyon. Carry a satellite communicator or downloaded maps for any backcountry travel.

intel.title: Strategic Stops
intel.text: Fuel is available in Garden Valley and Idaho City, but large gaps exist between forest service roads. Never enter the interior forest with less than a half-tank.

intel.title: Snowpack Access
intel.text: High-elevation roads to lakes like Deadwood often remain snowed-in until late June. Consult the Forest Service ranger station for current gate status before planning.

intel.title: Permits and Fees
intel.text: While general forest access is open, specific activities like commercial rafting or lookout stays require fees. Dispersed camping has a 14-day limit in most areas.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Boise Air Terminal, rent a high-clearance vehicle, and stock up at a full-service grocer before leaving the city limits.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance 4WD is strongly recommended for unpaved forest service roads; check rental terms for off-pavement use.
plan.goldenHour: Trinity Mountain Lookout offers immense sunset views over the Sawtooths, subject to clear summer skies.
